messages:
Alex: hey team — quick API contract question. i'm proposing we add detailed cached token counts to the /usage response so billing + customers can reconcile prompt vs completion vs cached. thinking of a new opt-in query param `detailed_usage=true`. thoughts?

Maria: +1 to having the counts, will help customers. main Q: opt-in vs always-on? bandwidth and privacy concerns. also need to agree on field names.

JC: +1 on opt-in. if we add fields by default we risk breaking clients that do strict schema validation. opt-in via query param or header is fine. suggestion: `?detailed_usage=true` for API and `X-Redwood-Detailed-Usage: 1` header for SDKs.

Kelsey: agree opt-in. also consider a single stable `chargeable_units` field that billing consumes — we should guarantee that never changes until we give advance notice. detailed fields can be added/changed.

Alex: good point re: chargeable_units. proposal for response snippet:

```
{
  "prompt_tokens": 120,
  "completion_tokens": 30,
  "cached_prefix_tokens": 50,
  "cached_completion_tokens": 0,
  "chargeable_units": 100
}
```

Maria: naming nit: `cached_prefix_tokens` vs `cached_input_tokens`? i'd prefer `cached_prompt_tokens` to stay consistent with `prompt_tokens`. also add `cache_hit_reason`? maybe overkill.

JC: +1 on `cached_prompt_tokens`. we should document definition: prompt_tokens = tokens actually processed (not served from cache), cached_prompt_tokens = tokens served from prefix/KV cache so not billed. completion_tokens similar.

Kelsey: need to handle streaming edge-case: when we stream and use kv-cache for middle tokens, do we count them as cached_completion_tokens right away? billing will need deterministic rules. my call: count cache hits when emitted to client (i.e., not charged).

billing-bot: heads up from accounting: our ledger expects `chargeable_units` = tokens we invoice. we cannot switch semantics mid-month. if you add new fields, ensure `chargeable_units` is computed the same as today unless we ship an explicit billing change and migration plan. :rotating_light:

Alex: noted. plan: keep `chargeable_units` stable. detailed fields are additive and opt-in. we'll add docs and changelog note. can someone own the API + SDK changes?

JC: I'll own API surface and schema PR. will add `detailed_usage` param and wire up header. i'll also add a compatibility test that ensures responses without the flag do not contain the new fields.

Maria: i'll update docs + examples and add a short note in the changelog about semantics and billing.

Kelsey: i'll write the billing test vectors and a small validator that compares `chargeable_units` to derived value from the detailed fields (when provided) and raises if mismatch. put in repo under `billing/tests/usage_recon`.

Alex: timeline?

JC: aiming for PR this week, deploy to staging early next week. SDK patches to read header/param will follow.

Maria: can we include a sample SDK call in the docs that shows `detailed_usage=true` and parsing the returned fields? i'll draft it.

Kelsey: edge-case: cached tokens from prefix merging across requests for the same session — ensure we only count the delta per request. i'll write that as a test case.

Alex: thanks. action items: JC -> open PR for API + opt-in flag, Maria -> docs + SDK examples, Kelsey -> billing tests, Alex -> coordinate rollout and send heads-up to enterprise customers. tagging @Maria @JC @Kelsey. :+1:

billing-bot: note: please include a migration note in the PR that says "no change to `chargeable_units` semantics; detailed fields are opt-in and for reconciliation only" so accounting can approve quickly.

JC: will do. thanks all.

Alex: closing loop — once PR is up i'll post link here for quick review. :eyes:
